test_title: PYST 1: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

She was accused (1) / with stealing the money (2) / by the cashier (3) / at the bank(4).
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the preposition "**with**" in part (2) of the sentence.
 
• Certain verbs are followed by specific fixed prepositions; the verb "**accused**" must always be followed by the preposition "**of**" when referring to a crime or wrongdoing.
 
• The construction "accused with" is grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**accused of stealing the money**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She was **accused of stealing the money** by the cashier at the bank."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "She was accused"** – This is the correct passive voice construction of the verb.
 
• **3: "by the cashier"** – This correctly identifies the agent performing the action in the passive voice.
 
• **4: "at the bank"** – This is a correct prepositional phrase indicating the location of the incident.
 
• **Confusing Pair:** It is important to distinguish between "**accused of**" and "**charged with**." While they have similar meanings, "charged" requires the preposition "with" (e.g., *She was charged with stealing*).
